status: DIAGNOSTIC -- CALIB only, no retraining, no EVAL, no new model
question: If every cell had its own kappa_c chosen with full knowledge of the CALIB labels, could the frozen gates be satisfied?
ORACLE_CAVEAT: Thresholds are chosen using the labels they are scored against. This is an UPPER BOUND on achievable per-cell performance; any honest procedure does strictly worse.
decomposition_note: Exact, not approximate: cells partition the states and the over-commitment denominator is fixed, so minimising total tied commits means minimising each cell independently under its own coverage floor.
reading: o*_min = 0.3455 exceeds the 0.1 ceiling even with oracle knowledge of the labels. Per-cell thresholds CANNOT fix this. The problem is not that cells sit on different score scales -- the resolvability representation does not separate ties sharply enough within cells. The next problem is REPRESENTATION, not calibration, and adding threshold machinery would be wasted effort.
does_not_alter: the frozen CALIBRATION_FAILED verdicts of probe 1 or probe 2

WHY_THE_ORACLE_FAILS_AUC_DECOMPOSITION.the_finding: The global AUC of 0.7041 is largely a BETWEEN-cell effect. The resolvability head learned that some regimes are more resolvable than others -- which is real, useful, and consistent with D4/D5 -- but WITHIN a cell it barely discriminates, at a pair-weighted mean AUC of 0.5449 with 5 of 15 cells below chance.
WHY_THE_ORACLE_FAILS_AUC_DECOMPOSITION.why_this_makes_per_cell_thresholds_futil: A per-cell kappa removes precisely the between-cell information the global number depended on. What remains inside each cell is near-chance ordering, so no set of per-cell cutoffs -- even oracle ones -- can trade coverage against over-commitment efficiently. This is why o*_min = 0.3455 rather than something near the ceiling.
WHY_THE_ORACLE_FAILS_AUC_DECOMPOSITION.what_the_model_actually_learned: A regime-level base rate, not a state-level resolvability judgement. It can say 'late stolen-flag states tend to be unresolvable'. It cannot say 'THIS state is unresolvable'.
WHY_THE_ORACLE_FAILS_AUC_DECOMPOSITION.consequence_for_the_next_experiment: The deficit is representational. Improving it requires a resolvability signal that discriminates WITHIN a regime, which the frozen Q_psi trunk -- fit on terminal margin, and shown capacity-limited in stolen-flag states by D2 -- may simply not encode. Threshold machinery of any kind is the wrong lever.
